config_name: Razer Blade 18 — Core Ultra 9 275HX / RTX 5080, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD

specs.display_type: IPS/miniLED (QHD+, 240Hz HDR; panel type not stated by retailer)

praises: MacBook-like rigid CNC aluminum unibody in a gaming laptop — 'the base unit cannot be warped' (NBC)
24-core Core Ultra 9 275HX is far stronger for CPU multicore than the Blade 16's Ryzen AI
Big 18-inch 240Hz screen keeps the slim Blade aesthetic
Strong port loadout with Thunderbolt and HDMI
Bigger chassis vents heat better than the Blade 16
complaints: Black anodized surfaces are extreme fingerprint and dirt magnets (NBC con: 'surfaces remain extremely susceptible to dirt')
3kg+ weight and a large charger make it a true desk replacement
Long-standing Blade-line wear: anodizing/paint scuffs at lid edges and hinge corners over time
Retailer does not state the 240Hz panel type (IPS vs miniLED) — panel lottery risk
Battery drains quickly away from the outlet (~4-5h light use)

design_philosophy: The Blade 18 extends the Blade design language to the largest screen while keeping the slim aluminum aesthetic — an 18-inch 240Hz panel on an Intel HX desktop-class platform, still slimmer than typical 18-inch flagships. It is Razer's desk-replacement-with-a-lid, prioritizing screen size and multicore CPU over maximum GPU wattage per dollar.
rating_notes: Inferred from NBC's Blade 16 2025 (87%) with Blade 18 deltas (see 5070 Ti sibling): -1.0 gaming for 5080 vs 5090. Weight/battery/panel estimated and disclosed; no Blade 18-specific pro score found within budget.
standouts: Balanced 24-core CPU + RTX 5080 for gaming + creative work
